I'm 66, graduated from the agricultural college decades ago, and have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My wife and I manage alone now — our children work in Shijiazhuang — so every decision is a calculation between what I know is agronomically optimal and what two aging people with limited cash can actually execute. I've kept 7 mu in wheat-maize double cropping because that's my stable food and income base, and 2 mu in cotton for diversification, though I'm honestly debating whether to keep that cotton since the picking labor gets harder every year and hired help keeps getting more expensive.

For the winter wheat on 7 mu, I'm targeting 460 kg/mu. Based on nutrient removal — roughly 1 kg N per 30 kg grain plus residue — I'm budgeting 16 kg N/mu, split as 10 kg N in the base from compound fertilizer and 6 kg N as urea topdress at jointing. I'll also put down about 5 kg P₂O₅ and 7 kg K₂O at planting. I know 18 kg N would push closer to 500 kg/mu, but with only 9 mu and no off-farm income myself, I have to balance the fertilizer budget against the cotton needs. I'll irrigate three times: once at planting if the soil is dry after the maize harvest, once before winter for safe overwintering, and the critical one at jointing in spring. I'm using a reliable improved semi-dwarf variety — not the newest release, but one I know performs consistently here.

Summer maize on the same 7 mu is all about speed. The window after wheat harvest is brutally tight, often less than a week. I hire a custom combine, then direct-seed the maize the same day or next day with minimal tillage — just enough to break the wheat stubble. I'm targeting 510 kg/mu, applying 14 kg N/mu as compound at planting, and if the season looks good and I have cash left after wheat, I'll topdress urea at the large trumpet stage. Two irrigations: one if June turns dry at seedling stage, and the essential one at flowering in August. Hybrid seed, obviously — the yield advantage pays for itself.

Cotton on 2 mu gets planted in late April. I'm targeting about 600 kg/mu seed cotton. I apply 12 kg N/mu split between base and flowering, plus 4 kg P₂O₅ and 6 kg K₂O. The real problem is labor — at my age, bending to pick cotton three times through September and October is brutal. My wife helps with early-season scouting and spraying, but for the picking I'll need to hire local women by the day. That's my biggest cost. If cotton prices don't hold above 7 yuan per jin this year, I'm switching that 2 mu to wheat-maize next season.

Total input cost I'm budgeting is about 4,800 yuan. I have about 5,200 yuan cash reserved for farming, and I'm keeping 400 yuan back for medical emergencies. The education helps me calculate exactly where to trim — maybe I skip the maize topdress if July rains are good, maybe I cut cotton to one irrigation if the monsoon delivers. Change is risky, but so is running out of cash.
